name: Bratmobile
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Two dorm neighbors in Eugene started a zine, then a band that didn't have instruments yet. They broke up mid-show in New York in 1994, then came back for two more records.

eras.title: A fake band with a zine
eras.text: Allison Wolfe and Molly Neuman meet in a dorm hallway, start the fanzine Girl Germs and play a show before they own instruments. By the end of 1991 they're a trio, and the only band to play the International Pop Underground Convention twice.

years.h: Wolfe walks into a dorm hallway and finds Neuman hogging the pay phone
years.p: [[Allison Wolfe|6ae4e39e-45fc-4276-94cd-bf149c20f7b9]] (from Olympia) and [[Molly Neuman|e4832571-a120-46fb-a5ff-1350f5ed2fce]] (from Washington, D.C.) both arrive in Eugene with activist families and a taste for punk, hip-hop and Beat Happening.
years.xp:
Wolfe has said she first noticed Neuman on the hallway's one pay phone, mid breakup, with a fast-talking East Coast accent. Neuman says the tears were about a summer romance ending.

Wolfe brought Olympia's K Records scene with her; Neuman brought Washington, D.C.

years.h: Neuman photocopies Girl Germs #1 in a congressman's office
years.p: Over winter break, Wolfe and Neuman put out the first issue in the Capitol Hill office of Arizona Representative Mo Udall.
years.xp:
It started as an idea for a radio show that never happened. The zine ran interviews with bands such as 7 Year Bitch, Jawbox and Unrest, and pieces from [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] and Mecca Normal's Jean Smith.

Copies now sit in archives at Duke, Barnard and the GLBT Historical Society in San Francisco.

q: We can't really play instruments exactly, but maybe we have something to say.
years.h: Calvin Johnson books a band that has no instruments yet
years.p: At Olympia's North Shore Surf Club, Wolfe and Neuman sing five a cappella songs, then borrow gear from Robert Christie of Some Velvet Sidewalk.
years.xp:
Wolfe's own phrase for the duo at that point was a "fake band." Christie lent them equipment and told them to listen to the Ramones; Wolfe decided to do the opposite and skip the Ramones on purpose.

KEXP's interview has them opening for [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]]. Neuman remembers it as Bikini Kill's second show; Wolfe says third. They recorded the next day for the first Kill Rock Stars compilation.

years.h: Spring break in D.C. adds Billotte, Smith and a basement tape
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman bring in guitarist [[Erin Smith|d497afe0-b769-4af3-9c85-a012a4d166a8]], drummer [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]] and artist Jen Smith, and rehearse at the Embassy, the Nation of Ulysses house.
years.xp: Calvin Johnson introduced Erin Smith to Neuman at a Nation of Ulysses show in December 1990. The D.C. group recorded in the Embassy basement with Tim Green and issued the cassette Bratmobile DC. Its first show was at Maxwell's in Hoboken, New Jersey, on an East Coast tour.

years.cap: Allison Wolfe, Erin Smith and Molly Neuman
years.h: Neuman moves to drums, Smith takes guitar, and Bratmobile is a trio
years.p: Wolfe sings. This is the lineup behind every Kill Rock Stars record.

years.h: Only Bratmobile get two sets at the Olympia convention
years.p: At the International Pop Underground Convention they play twice, including a Capitol Lake Park bill with the Melvins, Mecca Normal, Girl Trouble, Beat Happening and Fugazi.

eras.title: Pottymouth, then a stage turns into a fight
eras.text: The trio tours with Heavens to Betsy, records for John Peel and lands on Kill Rock Stars. It ends on a New York stage in the middle of an argument.

years.h: A summer tour with Heavens to Betsy leads to a split 7-inch
years.p: Bratmobile go out on the road with [[Heavens to Betsy|8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e]], and the friendship produces a record together.
years.xp: Split singles with Tiger Trap, Heavens to Betsy, Brainiac and Veronica Lake are part of the early catalog.

years.h: Tim Green works for a slice of cheese pizza and a bottle of black hair dye
years.p: Green, of Nation of Ulysses, records most of Pottymouth at the Embassy and takes that as payment.
years.xp: The album was pieced together over sessions from August 1991 to July 1992. Three songs came earlier from Egg Studios in Seattle and YoYo Studios in Olympia.

yt: Live at the Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, June 27, 1993
years.h: Pottymouth fits 17 songs into 27 minutes and change
years.p: The debut album on Kill Rock Stars runs 27:47. Robert Christgau singled out tracks, and AllMusic's Stewart Mason called it a snapshot of the early-90s indie scene.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes retrospective rankings, including a place on Rolling Stone's 2026 greatest punk albums list.

years.h: Four songs for John Peel at the BBC, out on Strange Fruit the next January
years.p: The session becomes The Peel Session, released in January 1994.
years.xp: The EP holds "There's No Other Way/No You Don't," "Bitch Theme," "Make Me Miss America" and "Panik."

years.h: The Real Janelle brings in Slim Moon to sing a Misfits song
years.p: Recorded at Avast in Seattle in July 1993, the six-song EP covers the Misfits with Kill Rock Stars co-founder Slim Moon on vocals.
years.xp: The cover shows Janelle Hessig, a former Bratmobile roadie and East Bay zine maker. AllMusic called the EP harder and tighter than the chaotic Pottymouth, a big step up.

q: Best performance art I've ever seen.
years.h: Thread Waxing Space turns into an argument, and the band ends there
years.p: At a hyped New York show, women in the crowd take the mic to confront a man in the audience, arguments spread, and Bratmobile break up in the chaos.
years.xp:
KEXP reports Sonic Youth, Joan Jett and Pussy Galore were in the room. Neuman had flown cross-country, slept on the plane and played a few hours later. Wolfe says she was suddenly expected to be talent, club manager and security at once: "It was like slapstick comedy... and we just broke up."

Spin's Ann Powers wrote that the stoppage lasted at least as long as the set.

eras.title: Neuman goes west, Wolfe stays east
eras.text: Neuman moves to the Bay Area and works at Lookout! Records; Wolfe stays in D.C. and starts a band with Erin Smith. The friendships outlast the breakup.

years.h: Wolfe and Smith stay in D.C. and start Cold Cold Hearts
years.p: Allison Wolfe and Erin Smith put out a 7-inch on Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp:
The band ran roughly 1995 to 1998 with drummer Katherine Brown and bassist Nattles. Its catalog is one 7-inch and one self-titled album (1997).

Meanwhile [[Molly Neuman|e4832571-a120-46fb-a5ff-1350f5ed2fce]] moved to the Bay Area, worked at Lookout! Records and played in [[The PeeChees|925ab37f-066e-4c7b-a390-e74df8bf7acd]].

eras.title: Back on Lookout!
eras.text: The trio reunites, tours with Sleater-Kinney and makes two records for Lookout!, the label Neuman co-owns. By 2004 day jobs win.

years.h: A backstage hello in D.C., then the Stork Club in Oakland
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman reconnect at a D.C. show where Neuman is managing the Donnas. A low-key Oakland gig relaunches the band, which tours with Sleater-Kinney.
years.xp: Neuman remembers someone telling them Bratmobile was in the building: "Oh, hey, we are." Wolfe points out the break lasted only about four years, which felt much longer in your twenties.

years.h: Six years after The Real Janelle, Ladies, Women and Girls
years.p: Recorded with Tim Green and released on Lookout! Records, with Jon Nikki adding bass and keyboards. It charts at No. 22 on CMJ.
years.xp: Rolling Stone said the Brat spirit was fully intact. Pitchfork gave it 6.8 out of 10 and Spin 7.

years.h: Audrey Marrs brings keyboards to Girls Get Busy
years.p: [[Audrey Marrs|d08e65b1-b0f5-406d-a63e-da1abba95d7d]] joins on keys and backing vocals and Marty Violence plays bass on the Lookout! Records album, which charts at No. 17 on CMJ.
years.xp: Reviews split: Pitchfork gave it 4.9, Alternative Press 7 out of 10. Wikipedia credits Marty Key with production alongside Aaron Prellwitz.

years.h: No announcement, just a message-board post
years.p: Wolfe writes it on the band's message board. Nobody had quit; Neuman was running Lookout! and managing the Donnas and the Locust, Smith worked at Lookout!, and Wolfe had two part-time jobs.
years.xp: Wolfe wrote that there was never a moment when anyone said "I quit," and that all three just had different ways of doing things. She named her side projects as Hawnay Troof, Baby Truth and [[Partyline|cbc09303-767e-4247-83c8-41c26664726c]].

eras.title: Girl Germs, again
eras.text: A podcast, a birthday-party show, festival stages and two reissues bring the songs back around.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars turns the band's story into a Girl Germs podcast
years.p: The label names the series after the zine.

years.h: The original trio plays [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]]'s birthday party
years.p: Wolfe, Neuman and Smith play together again at Tobi Vail's party.

years.h: Mosswood Meltdown puts Bratmobile back on stage in Oakland
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman reform with Tiger Trap's Rose Melberg, Audrey Marrs and Marty Key. Erin Smith is unavailable.
years.xp: Neuman told KEXP the two living in the same town now was one reason it made sense to try. Their goal: "we want to have some fun."

years.cap: Bratmobile at the Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 20, 2024
years.h: Wolfe says she's nervous and excited before Union Park
years.p: Pitchfork Music Festival in Chicago is one of the band's first shows in 20 years; the band says the old songs still apply.
years.xp: Asked about new music, the band says it prefers to play the older songs well for now. Wolfe talks about the need for different voices in turbulent times, and "dancing at the revolution."

years.h: Ladies, Women and Girls and Girls Get Busy come home to Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Both Lookout!-era albums are reissued on the Kill Rock Stars label.
years.xp: Neuman said the band was revisiting the records and hearing them in a new way. On new music, she said it's "not a plan right now."

sources.title: KEXP: Throwaway Style, an interview with Bratmobile
